title: Near-atomistic simulations reveal the molecular principles that control chromatin structure and phase separation
task: Predict chromatin structure and phase separation from molecular principles
key_results: OpenCGChromatin simulates chromatin fibers up to 108 nucleosomes; predicts linker-DNA-dependent structures matching cryo-ET observations; identifies H4K16 and H3K9 acetylation as most disruptive modifications to compaction
comments: Impressive scale-up enables bridging atomistic detail to mesoscale organization, though validation beyond cryo-ET and biochemical assays remains limited.

model_io.model: OpenCGChromatin coarse-grained molecular dynamics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Linker-DNA length controls histone tail accessibility and chromatin condensate multiscale structure
hypotheses.result: Confirmed through simulations revealing length-dependent tail dynamics

hypotheses.hypothesis: Acetylation disrupts chromatin compaction in a pattern-specific manner
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; H4K16 and H3K9 modifications most energetically disruptive

title: The structural dynamics and molecular coupling in the slow inactivation of a prokaryotic voltage-gated sodium channel
task: Elucidate structural mechanism and molecular coupling in slow inactivation of voltage-gated sodium channels
key_results: Single-molecule FRET reveals selectivity filter transits among three conformational states; L176-T206 residue pair identified as steric-hindrance coupler controlling slow inactivation gate coupling
comments: Elegant integration of smFRET dynamics with crystallography and mutagenesis provides mechanistic insight, though direct structural visualization of the inactivated state remains elusive.

model_io.model: NavAb prokaryotic voltage-gated sodium channel

hypotheses.hypothesis: Selectivity filter serves as the inactivation gate with depolarization enriching slow-inactivated conformation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; depolarization enriches high FRET state consistent with SF closure

hypotheses.hypothesis: L176-T206 forms a steric-hindrance coupler linking primary and inactivation gates
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; L176F overrides opening tendency of ΔC230 and restores high FRET population; T206A partially uncouples gates

title: Wild-type and mutated ß-catenin differently repress RND3/RHOE expression in hepatocellular carcinoma
task: Determine whether wild-type and mutant β-catenin differentially regulate RND3 expression in hepatocellular carcinoma
key_results: Wild-type β-catenin suppresses RND3 transcription via Hippo pathway; oncogenic β-catenin downregulates RND3 via miR-512-3p targeting the 3'UTR
comments: The discovery of two distinct β-catenin-dependent mechanisms for RND3 repression indicates functional divergence between structural and transcriptional roles.

model_io.model: Human HCC samples and cultured hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines

hypotheses.hypothesis: Both structural and transcriptional functions of β-catenin independently repress RND3 in HCC
hypotheses.result: Wild-type β-catenin suppresses RND3 via Hippo pathway; oncogenic β-catenin via miR-512-3p-mediated 3'UTR targeting

title: p300/CBP inhibition promotes apoptosis in mouse embryos by impairing H1K75ac-associated DNA repair during the 4-cell-to-blastocyst transition
task: Elucidate the role of p300/CBP in mouse preimplantation embryonic development during 4-cell-to-blastocyst transition
key_results: p300/CBP inhibition reduced morula and blastocyst formation, increased embryonic fragmentation and apoptosis, impaired H1K75ac-mediated DNA repair, and accumulated DNA damage
comments: The mechanistic link between H1K75ac, ATM signaling, and developmental competence provides a clear epigenetic basis for preimplantation lethality.

model_io.model: Mouse preimplantation embryos (4-cell to blastocyst stage) with p300/CBP inhibition

hypotheses.hypothesis: p300/CBP promotes blastocyst formation through H1K75ac-mediated DNA repair and genomic stability
hypotheses.result: p300/CBP inhibition reduced H1K75ac, impaired DNA repair, accumulated DNA damage, and increased apoptosis

title: The FOS transcription factor negatively regulates MAFF to control myometrial cell contractility
task: Determine whether FOS negatively regulates MAFF to control myometrial contractility
key_results: FOS knockdown increased MAFF mRNA ~1.5–1.7-fold; MAFF-deficient cells showed 15–25% reduced basal contractility; MAFF overexpression increased contractility 4–8%; FOS overexpression reduced contractility by 6.7% in wild-type cells only
comments: The phenotype dependency on MAFF in FOS-overexpressing cells provides evidence for direct functional regulation rather than pleiotropic effects.

model_io.model: Human myometrial cells with FOS/MAFF knockdown or overexpression
outputs: ChIP-qPCR FOS binding to MAFF promoter

hypotheses.hypothesis: FOS negatively regulates MAFF expression to suppress myometrial contractility
hypotheses.result: FOS knockdown increased MAFF; FOS overexpression reduced contractility in MAFF-dependent manner

title: Fresh frozen plasma-based resuscitation lessens lung injury in mice with abdominal sepsis and hemorrhagic shock
task: Determine whether FFP or fibrinogen attenuates lung injury in combined abdominal sepsis and hemorrhagic shock
key_results: FFP significantly reduced alveolar thickness, restored lung syndecan-1, and decreased plasma neutrophil granule-enzymes (myeloperoxidase, neutrophil elastase, MMP9); fibrinogen showed no protective effect
comments: The differential efficacy between FFP and fibrinogen despite similar resuscitation volumes suggests FFP contains additional protective components beyond fibrinogen alone.

model_io.model: Mouse cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) + hemorrhagic shock

hypotheses.hypothesis: FFP and fibrinogen restore endothelial syndecan-1 and reverse endothelial injury in combined sepsis and hemorrhagic shock
hypotheses.result: FFP attenuated syndecan-1 shedding and lung injury; fibrinogen did not

title: The long non-coding RNA LINC00276-202 regulates RPE differentiation through hnRNPL and β-catenin-associated signaling
task: Determine the role of lncRNA LINC00276-202 in retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) differentiation through miRNA and protein interactions
key_results: LINC00276-202 silencing reduced RPE65/MITF/TRPM1/TRPM3 expression; miR-204/miR-211 modestly increased reporter activity via seed region; hnRNPL binding validated by RNA-IP; hnRNPL regulated β-catenin levels and TCF/LEF activity
comments: The modest effect of miRNA-responsive elements compared to hnRNPL interaction suggests protein scaffolding may be the primary regulatory mechanism.

model_io.model: Human ARPE-19 retinal pigment epithelial cells during differentiation with LINC00276-202 modulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: LINC00276-202 regulates RPE differentiation through miR-204/miR-211-responsive elements and hnRNPL-mediated β-catenin signaling
hypotheses.result: LINC00276-202 silencing impaired RPE gene expression; hnRNPL interaction and β-catenin signaling mediated its effects

title: Harnessing cell cycle synchronization to boost the therapeutic potential of umbilical cord MSCs against acute colitis
task: Determine whether cell cycle synchronization of umbilical cord mesenchymal stromal cells (UCMSCs) enhances therapeutic efficacy in acute colitis
key_results: S-phase and G2/M-phase cells showed increased proliferation potential; synchronized UCMSCs significantly attenuated DSS-induced colon shortening, promoted histological restoration, and reduced inflammatory infiltration compared to non-synchronized cells
comments: The enhanced efficacy was associated with synchronization itself rather than a specific phase, suggesting that developmental uniformity optimizes therapeutic function.

model_io.model: Human UCMSCs synchronized to G0/G1, S, or G2/M phases and administered to DSS-induced acute colitis mice

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cell cycle synchronization of UCMSCs enhances therapeutic efficacy in acute colitis by optimizing immunomodulatory function
hypotheses.result: Synchronized UCMSCs reduced disease severity, colon damage, and inflammatory infiltration more effectively than non-synchronized cells

title: LMOD2 attenuates Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy by activating the Nrf2-mediated antioxidant pathway
task: Determine whether LMOD2 suppresses Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy via Nrf2-mediated antioxidant signaling
key_results: LMOD2 overexpression decreased hypertrophic markers (ANP, BNP, MYH7) by ~50%, reduced ROS/MDA/4-HNE, increased GSH, and promoted Nrf2 nuclear accumulation; Nrf2 inhibitor ML385 abolished LMOD2 protection

hypotheses.hypothesis: LMOD2 attenuates Ang II-induced hypertrophy by activating Nrf2-mediated antioxidant defenses
hypotheses.result: LMOD2 overexpression upregulated Nrf2 targets and reduced oxidative stress; Nrf2 inhibition abolished LMOD2 protection

comments: Assembly-based approach outperforms alignment methods for complex loci but 8% failure rate on XX individuals limits applicability; method-specific technical threshold for clinical implementation.

title: Interpretable survival prediction in Parkinson’s disease with AI-assisted web deployment
task: Develop interpretable Cox regression survival model for Parkinson's disease with web deployment
key_results: Cox model (11 predictors) achieved mean C-index 0.716 in cross-validation; mean 2-, 4-, 6-year AUCs 0.713, 0.726, 0.750; temporal validation C-index 0.708; model deployed in web platform for individualized survival estimates (3148 PD patients, 19 hospitals, 2018–2024)
comments: Robust Cox model with reasonable discrimination and web deployment is clinically pragmatic, but modest underestimation of absolute mortality risk in temporal validation warrants recalibration before clinical use.

model_io.model: Cox proportional hazards + multiple imputation
inputs: PD patient data (demographic, genetic, treatment, motor, non-motor domains)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Parsimonious Cox model with 11 predictors across demographic, genetic, treatment, and motor/non-motor domains predicts PD survival
hypotheses.result: C-index 0.716 (cross-validation), 0.708 (temporal validation); AUCs 0.713–0.750 at 2–6 years

key_results: SHA-256 hashing 0.365 ± 0.006 s for 3,151 files; Merkle-tree construction 0.0073 ± 0.0006 s; Merkle-proof verification 0.0486 ± 0.002 ms; AES-256 decryption 0.33 ± 0.05 ms per file; hashing scaling R²=0.992
comments: Cryptographic feasibility established but end-to-end blockchain workflow (approval, revocation, guardian recovery) not fully implemented; watermark vulnerable to geometric distortions; reactive post-distribution attribution is a fundamental limitation.

title: CrossCD-Eval: a unified framework with domain-aware feature normalization for cross-domain remote sensing change detection
task: Evaluate deep learning change detection models under cross-domain remote sensing with feature normalization
key_results: CrossCD-Eval framework tested 5 models on 3 datasets; all degrade under cross-domain transfer; Domain-Aware Feature Normalization (DAFN) improved performance with up to 22.7% IoU std. dev. reduction; DAFN outperformed preprocessing, AdaBN, adversarial alignment, and instance-norm baseline
comments: Domain shift quantification and DAFN lightweight adaptation is practical, but evaluation limited to three datasets; generalization to other remote-sensing tasks unclear.

model_io.model: Deep learning change detection (GLAFormer, Change-Mamba, EHCTNet, ELGC-Net, STNet) + DAFN
inputs: Remote sensing image pairs (CLCD, HRSCD, LEVIR-CD)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Domain-aware feature normalization reduces representation-level mismatch and improves cross-domain change detection generalization
